'''''Mnium hornum''''', also known by the common names '''horn calcareous moss''' or '''swan's-neck thyme-moss''', is a [[species]] of [[moss]] in the [[genus]] ''[[Mnium]]''.<ref>[[Johann Hedwig|Hedwig]]. Sp. Musc. Frond. (1801).</ref>

==Description==
The upright stems of swan's-neck thyme-moss are 2 to 4 cm tall. Leaves are 4mm to 8mm long, with a toothed border of long, narrow cells. The [[Leaf#Veins|vein]] ends a slightly below the tip of the leaf. The lower part of the stem has small, narrow triangular leaves. [[Capsule (fruit)|Capsules]] are 5mm long, with a lid that narrows abruptly into a short point. The [[seta]] is between 2.5 and 5 cm long.<ref name=BryoFactSheet>{{cite web|url=https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Mnium-hornum.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230728150233/https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Mnium-hornum.pdf|archive-date=28 July 2023|language=en-GB|url-status=live|title= Mnium hornum - Swan's-neck thyme-moss|access-date=28 July 2023}}</ref>

==Habitat==
Swan's-neck thyme-moss is native to Europe and eastern North America.
It is commonly found in damp woodland conditions, especially in acidic soil, such as oak-birch, beech and pine woodlands. It is found on the ground, logs, rocks, tree bases and along streams.<ref name=WoodlandTrust>{{cite web|url=https://www.woodlandtrust.org.uk/trees-woods-and-wildlife/plants/mosses/swans-neck-thyme-moss|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230728150659/https://www.woodlandtrust.org.uk/trees-woods-and-wildlife/plants/mosses/swans-neck-thyme-moss/|archive-date=28 July 2023|language=en-GB|url-status=live|title= SWAN'S-NECK THYME-MOSS (Mnium hornum)|access-date=28 July 2023}}</ref>

==Uses==
In 2012, researchers in Serbia found that ''Mnium hornum'' could be used as a potential source of [[arachidonic acid]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pejin |first1=B |last2=Vujisic |first2=Lj |last3=Sabovljevic |first3=M |last4=Tesevic |first4=V |last5=Vajs |first5=V |date=22 March 2012 |title=The moss Mnium hornum, a promising source of arachidonic acid |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10600-012-0175-7 |journal=Chemistry of Natural Compounds |volume=48 |issue= 1|pages=120–121 |doi=10.1007/s10600-012-0175-7 |bibcode=2012CNatC..48..120P |access-date=28 July 2023|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
